hooks.text: A glowing beam of energy shoots five thousand light-years across space.
How can a single black hole fire a jet across five thousand light-years?
Six point five billion suns are packed into one galaxy's central abyss.

title: The 5,000-Light-Year Ray From a Black Hole
description: Witness the scale of Messier 87, a galaxy firing a relativistic plasma jet powered by a 6.5-billion-solar-mass black hole.

beats.text: A glowing beam of energy shoots five thousand light-years across space.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope optical view of M87's relativistic plasma jet, 1999

beats.text: [Messier](/mˈɛsˈiˈI/) 87 is a massive galaxy with trillions of stars.
beats.visual: Wide-field optical view of giant elliptical galaxy Messier 87, 2010

beats.text: Fifty-five million light-years away, it dwarfs our Milky Way with fifteen thousand globular clusters.
beats.visual: Hubble image of globular clusters surrounding Messier 87, 2011

beats.text: In 1918, astronomer [Heber](/hˈibˈɜɹ/) Curtis of Lick Observatory spotted a bizarre straight ray erupting from the core.
beats.visual: Archival photograph of astronomer Heber Curtis at Lick Observatory, 1918

beats.text: The jet creates a trick, appearing to move faster than light.
beats.visual: Very Large Array radio map of Virgo A and the M87 radio lobes, 2015

beats.text: This optical illusion occurs as matter blasts toward Earth at nearly the speed of light.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope close-up of knots in the M87 jet, 1994

beats.text: It is powered by a black hole 6.5 billion times heavier than our sun.
beats.visual: Event Horizon Telescope historic first image of the M87 black hole shadow, 2019

beats.text: In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope revealed the first direct image of this gravitational monster's shadow.
beats.visual: Polarized light image of M87* showing magnetic field structure, 2021

beats.text: This massive anchor provides the raw power for the glowing beam of energy shooting across space.
